title: Prelude in C minor, Op. 28 No. 20
subtitle: "Funeral March"
trains: Dense, widely-spread four- and five-note block chords in both hands (up to a minor 10th), a full ff-to-pp dynamic range with two written crescendi, and a two-layer right-hand texture (a sustained chord against a decorative turn figure) that asks for careful voicing and pedalling rather than finger speed.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Frédéric Chopin, Prelude in C minor, Op. 28 No. 20 (composed 1838/39, public domain). Transcribed from the Mutopia Project's public-domain LilyPond source (piece-info id 472, Chop-28-20.ly, typeset by Magnus Lewis-Smith from the Edition Peters plate).
provenance.note: Every pitch in this file was derived mechanically, not by ear or by eye: the raw Chop-28-20.ly source was downloaded and its \relative-octave note tokens were decoded with a small verification script implementing LilyPond's own documented relative-pitch algorithm (including the 'a chord's first note is relative to the first note of the preceding chord' rule, confirmed against the current LilyPond Notation Reference before use), then cross-checked bar-by-bar against the Mutopia PDF engraving and against two independent published harmonic-analysis summaries of the piece (Wikipedia's article on this Prelude; a bar-by-bar analysis site) for macro-level sanity (chord roots, the C-minor-to-A-flat-major opening move, the return to the tonic). One transcription slip was caught this way: the left hand's measure 9 was first copied verbatim from measure 5's identical-looking text, but measure 9's first chord actually carries an extra explicit octave mark in the source (<c' c'> vs measure 5's <c c'>) that resets the register for the reprise - missing it produced a left hand that drifted down below the piano's range by measure 12. Fixed by re-diffing every 'repeated' measure against its source text character-by-character rather than assuming a repeat. Tempo (Largo, quarter = 42), dynamics (ff/p/pp, two crescendi, one riten., 'a tempo'), and the clef changes between the two staves are also taken from the source. The source's near-continuous, retaken-every-chord sustain pedal is simplified in this file to a single pedal-down at the first note and pedal-up at the final chord, rather than encoding dozens of individual retakes (see limitations).

limitations: Written pedal is not played by the engine (facts.hasPedal is informational only).

The source's pedal is retaken on nearly every chord throughout; this file encodes only a single sustained pedal-down/pedal-up pair spanning the whole piece rather than every individual retake, for encoding simplicity.

Slurs and the exact hairpin start/stop beat positions from the source engraving are approximated, not reproduced to the exact beat; they do not change the sounding pitches, rhythm or overall dynamic shape.
